why: Both G4 consumers pin an exact 3.0.0-next.N read from floors.G4.next, and N does not exist on npm until the owner cuts it. Without this row the consumers start against an unpublished version and fail their frozen install.
what: Owner row, no code. The owner runs make release from master after v3-freeze-g4 merges; no lead builds or releases anything.
contract: concepts/migration-release.md 4.4 (one cut per gate exit, reason stated) and 3.3 (floors, gaFloor). Only make release; never dispatch a workflow by hand. N is whatever the registry takes: any other cut (a blocked-consumer cut, a G2 or G3 cut) landing first moves it.
exemplar: v3-rel-2-release-2-29-1 (owner row shape, acceptance by npm view).
change: Owner: run make release-dry and read N from the 3.0.0-next.N it prints. If N equals floors.G4.next in scripts/fleet.json, run make release with the reason 'G4 charts API and bundle marginals frozen'. If it differs, do not release yet: set floors.G4.next and gaFloor to the printed N in one chore commit (chore: align G4 fleet floor with the cut), merge it, then release. A green exit means the registry serves it. If the Issue is filed to a lead, the lead only verifies the acceptance lines read-only and signals; it must not run make release.
commits: None from the release (semantic-release writes its own). At most one chore: align G4 fleet floor with the cut.
proof: npm view output below; the Publish run log carries --tag next.
acceptance: npm view basalt-ui dist-tags.next prints 3.0.0-next.N where N equals floors.G4.next in scripts/fleet.json on master.
gaFloor in scripts/fleet.json on master is at or above floors.G4.next.
git ls-remote --tags origin v3.0.0-next.N returns a ref.
out_of_scope: Any other file change, consumer bumps (v3-g4-weatherorb, v3-g4-image), fleet-status --probe, a 3.0.0 release.
